chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān from Sā'īn al-A'raj who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no mut'ah (compensation for missing a ritual) for the people of Sarif, nor for the people of Marr, nor for the people of Mecca,'
as Allah the Exalted says: 'That is for him whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ سَرِفٍ: The people of Sarif, a specific location near Mecca
key_terms.أَهْلِ مَرٍّ: The people of Marr, a specific location near Mecca
key_terms.حاضِرِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرامِ: Those present at the Sacred Mosque
key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: Compensation or offering given for missing a specific ritual requirement in Hajj

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from paying compensation (mut'ah) for missing Hajj rituals according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) exempts the residents of Mecca and its immediate vicinity (Sarif and Marr) from the *mut'ah* compensation for missing Hajj rituals, distinguishing them from pilgrims traveling from afar. This ruling is derived from the Quranic phrase 'those whose families are not present at the Sacred Mosque,' establishing a legal precedent where local residents are considered to have fulfilled the obligation through proximity rather than the specific sacrificial compensation required of distant pilgrims.
